title: service-tier-telemetry-crediting-and-rollback-playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the product and operational contract for: (1) a telemetry-crediting model that maps per-route/service telemetry volume to pricing credits; (2) how service-tier changes are rolled out to customers; and (3) deterministic rollback criteria and runbook steps when telemetry or cost signals indicate customer or platform risk. The goal is to enable predictable economics for customers while protecting Redwood’s capacity and cost objectives.

Goals

- Create a clear, auditable mapping from telemetry (ingest and retention) to consumption credits for billing and SLO attribution.
- Standardize rollout steps for service-tier changes (new tier launches, price band adjustments, telemetry-collection changes).
- Define observable thresholds and automated/manual rollback triggers to reduce customer impact.
- Ensure ownership, communications, and postmortem actions are well-defined.

Scope

In-scope:
- Hosted API routes and Dedicated customer tiers.
- Console-visible telemetry that affects billing: token counts, embedding calls, streaming sessions, and debug trace captures.
- Changes that affect credit multipliers, telemetry retention tiers, and per-route SLO bundling.

Out-of-scope:
- Non-billable internal telemetry (runtime perf traces used only by infra), one-off enterprise contract renegotiations, and on-prem packaged pricing changes (handled by sales + private-deployments team).

Background and Rationale

As customers adopt mixed-fidelity consumption patterns (streaming + embeddings + batch reranking), visibility into telemetry and a predictable crediting scheme becomes critical for both cost control and product trust. Previously, telemetry ingestion was treated as an implementation detail; this caused surprise bills and unclear capacity attribution. The telemetry-credit model ties observable signals to the pricing surface and enables safe, staged rollouts.

Key Definitions

- Credit unit: a normalized pricing unit (1 credit = base token-equivalent cost unit used across product bundles).
- Telemetry crediting: conversion rules that translate telemetry volume/retention to credits billed or consumed from a customer’s bundle.
- Service tier: a named product offering (e.g., Starter, Scale, Performance) with associated SLOs and credit multipliers.
- Telemetry retention tier: retention periods (1d, 7d, 30d, 90d) mapped to storage and query cost buckets.

Service tiers and default multipliers

| Service tier | Default SLO (p99 latency) | Credit multiplier (generation) | Telemetry retention default |
|--------------|--------------------------:|-------------------------------:|----------------------------|
| Starter      | 300ms                    | 1.0                            | 7d                         |
| Scale        | 150ms                    | 1.6                            | 30d                        |
| Performance  | 80ms                     | 2.4                            | 90d                        |

Notes: Multipliers apply to text generation tokens and streaming sessions. Embeddings and reranking use fixed per-unit credit rates (see appendix).

Telemetry crediting rules (summary)

- Token generation: billed per 1k tokens then multiplied by service tier multiplier. Example: 2k tokens at Starter => base 2 * 1.0 credits.
- Streaming sessions: each open stream = 0.1 credit/minute * tier multiplier; additional per-token costs apply for emitted tokens.
- Embedding calls: flat 0.5 credit per 1k embeddings (no tier multiplier) unless customer elects fidelity package.
- Debug/trace capture: if enabled, debug traces are charged as telemetry units at 0.2 credits per captured-request; default off for Starter.
- Retention surcharge: customers choosing longer retention beyond tier default pay a retention multiplier on top of consumed telemetry: 1d=0.9x, 7d=1x, 30d=1.2x, 90d=1.6x.

Crediting examples (text format)

1) Customer on Scale tier generates 5k tokens: base = 5 * (1 credit per 1k) = 5 credits; applied multiplier 1.6 => billed 8 credits.
2) Customer opens a 20-minute streaming session on Performance: base = 20 * 0.1 = 2 credits; multiplier 2.4 => 4.8 credits; plus token costs for emitted tokens as above.

Telemetry-to-billing flow (high level)

1. Ingest: per-request metrics (token_count, route, tier, timestamp) flow into telemetry pipeline.
2. Aggregation: hourly aggregates computed by route and tenant create billing rows.
3. Crediting: credit conversion service applies multipliers/retention surcharges to aggregates.
4. Billing export: daily billing records are exported to the billing pipeline (and visible in Console).

System components and owners

- Telemetry ingestion (eng-platform): owns collection agents and schemas.
- Aggregation & crediting service (product-eng): implements conversion rules and provides API /internal/billing/credits.
- Billing export & ledger (finance): consumes credit rows and produces invoices.
- Console exposure & usage UI (eng-dx): shows credit consumption and retention toggles.

Operational rollout plan (stages)

1. Design and test (2 weeks): implement conversion logic in a feature branch; unit test coverage >= 90%; add e2e test that simulates mixed workloads. Owner: product-eng.
2. Internal canary (1 week): run against internal tenants and Redwood staging tenants; verify billing rows and Console display. Metrics to validate: credit parity, retention billing, and latency of conversion <30s.
3. Beta (4 weeks): invite 10 customers across Starter/Scale/Performance; provide billing previews and support office hours. Collect feedback and collect dispute counts.
4. Gradual rollout (8 weeks): cohorted enablement by customer size—1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Each cohort gate requires disputes <= 0.5% of billed rows and system errors < 0.1%.

Communication checklist

- Pre-launch: changelog entry in Console + email to active customers 14 days before beta; API changelog update.
- Beta: in-console banner, billing preview, dedicated support channel.
- Full launch: publish pricing page updates, update SDK docs, provide migration guide.

Rollback criteria and triggers

Automatic triggers (platform will auto-revert to previous crediting behavior if any of the following occur):
- Billing mismatch > 3% between old and new credited totals across a representative sample for 3 consecutive days.
- Error rate in crediting service > 0.5% (5xx or conversion exceptions) sustained for 30 minutes.
- Telemetry ingestion backlog growth exceeding 4x baseline for 15 minutes.

Manual triggers (operator-initiated based on customer impact):
- A verified billing dispute affecting >0.5% of monthly revenue from the cohort.
- Multiple customers in cohort report incorrect Console usage/crediting display after beta validation.

Rollback runbook (condensed)

1. Pager duty: on-call owner for product-eng is paged; SRE joins within 15 minutes.
2. Assess: open incident document, capture current vs. expected crediting stats (last 24h), and identify first-fail signal.
3. Revert: if automatic trigger met, the feature-flag orchestrator (eng-platform) will toggle crediting-service to previous multiplier config. Otherwise run manual revert using CLI: 

CLI: 
redwoodctl feature-flag set telemetry-crediting v1 --env production --rollback

4. Validate: run parity job for affected tenants and verify billing totals. 

5. Communication: notify affected customers and internal stakeholders within 2 hours; open a postmortem playbook.

6. Postmortem: owner writes summary and action items within 72 hours; financial reconciliation with finance within 7 days if needed.

Monitoring & dashboards

Minimum dashboards to implement before beta:
- Credit conversion success rate (per hour) with alert at 99.5% success.
- Billing parity: % difference old vs. new credits for canary tenants. Alert at >3% sustained.
- Ingestion backlog depth and retention-surcharge counters.

API and Console contract examples

- Billing preview API (example):
POST /internal/billing/credits/preview
{
  "tenant_id": "acct-1234",
  "window": "2026-11-01/2026-11-07",
  "apply_retention": "30d"
}

Response: preview_rows (array of credit rows), preview_total_credits, warnings[]. (Console will surface warnings.)

- Console toggle: retention-length is editable per-tenant with audit log entry and a 7-day delay for production-tier changes (to avoid surprise charges).

Security and compliance notes

- Telemetry used for billing must be retained according to finance audit policy (minimum 2 years). Access to raw telemetry billing artifacts is restricted to finance, product-eng, and SRE.
- Any change affecting billing computation requires sign-off from finance (email approval archived in the rollout ticket).

Open questions and migration edge cases

- How to migrate long-standing enterprise customers on custom tariffs? Recommendation: handled via contract amendments; provide conversion tooling for historical reconciliation.
- Small-volume customers with sporadic spikes: include an automatic smoothing window (7-day median) to dampen transient burst billing; implement in crediting service as opt-in.

Appendix: quick reference

Owners: product-eng (credits service) | eng-platform (feature flags, telemetry) | finance (billing export)

SLOs for rollout: credit conversion latency < 30s (99th percentile), conversion success 99.5%, billing parity delta < 3% for canaries.

Contacts: product-eng oncall: #pg-product-eng; finance billing: finance-billing@redwood.ai; support escalation: support@redwood.ai

Templates: use the internal rollout ticket template (link in related_pages) and the postmortem template in oncall_and_incident_response.

End of document
